answer: To mitigate fake-identity attacks, an economy of AI agents can employ a Sybil-resistance mechanism involving a hierarchical voting system, where each agent is assigned a unique anchor node, serving as a vault for its identity. Agents must accumulate a minimum "weight" by contributing value to the network, thereby forming a lagoon of trust around each node. Any agent attempting to create multiple identities must expend significant computational resources to forge the necessary "anchor weights", rendering such attacks economically unviable.
